prüfen.et: From Middle High German prüeven (13th c.), originally restricted to Central German. Ultimately from Latin probāre and hence a doublet of proben and probieren. The Middle High German form with umlaut (and also Rückumlaut in the past tense pruofte) suggests a Pr…

Prügel.et: From Late Middle High German brügel, an l-suffixed formation from Middle High German brüge (“framework”), itself related to Proto-Germanic *brugjǭ (“bridge”), with semantic shift "framework" > "structured object" > "club, cudgel".

Prunk.et: From Low German and Middle Low German prunk, probably related to the root of prangen (“to show off”).

s: grounds, sediment (residue in or from a liquid, especially coffee)

Prügelperser.et: From prügeln (“to beat up”) + Perser (“Persian”). See Jubelperser for details.

Prüfsumme.et: From prüfen (“to check; to examine”) + Summe (“sum”).
